decisions.reason: F1 states the true ambient-cover equivalence but omits the lemma expressly required by def-compact-space. Step 1.1 instead uses singleton covers of the subspace K, so the actual finiteness proof and both topology inclusions are sound. Added the ambient compactness citation and dependency, its exact contract citation, and the owning manifest dependency.

Steps 2.1 and 4.1 take finite subcovers of L and delta0[L] from ambient open sets, but def-compact-space explicitly requires citing lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient. This missing dependency supports essential compact-lift and inverse-continuity steps. Added that supplier and finite choice in F9, their step tags, and the ambient criterion for the finite-union argument in F8; the claims and AC hypothesis are preserved.

The original step constructs (xi_1,...,xi_n), although def-p-norms-on-rn and lem-metrics-on-rn define vectors as functions on n with indices j<n. Thus xi_n was never supplied and xi_0 was omitted; that expression does not construct the claimed vector. Repaired F2 and steps 1.1-3.1 to use j<n and define xi(j)=xi_j. Added the actual standard-basis and inner-product suppliers instead of the unrelated group-power-law citation, and made the continuity-at-identity argument explicit.

reviews.reason: The singleton cover proves compact discrete K finite intrinsically; S(K,V) is then a finite intersection of coordinate constraints, and compact singleton constraints give the converse inclusion. Restriction preserves equality for every function family, including empty domains or targets. F1 now cites the actual ambient-compactness interface. Statement and page claims are unchanged; strict focused proof-contract check passed with zero errors and warnings.

Pullback preimages are S(phi[K],V); the quotient is open, Hausdorff and locally compact by closedness of H and images of compact neighbourhoods. AC chooses lift triples; the indexed ambient criterion supplies finitely many indices and compact union K with L contained in q[K]. Descent is bijective onto the closed annihilator. A finite target cover gives W with delta0(l)W contained in V, and translated S(K,W) proves inverse continuity. Empty L and H=0 or H=G are covered. Only facts, proof citations and dependencies change.

The standard basis is indexed on n; each coordinate character has a unique real frequency, so j maps to xi_j defines a vector without Choice. Decomposition and exponential addition give the classification, and testing each coordinate proves uniqueness. For nonempty compact K the continuous norm has finite maximum R; Cauchy-Schwarz and delta=delta-prime/(R+1) give continuity, including R=0. If norm(eta)>=epsilon, x=eta/(2 norm(eta)^2) lies in the compact radius-1/(2 epsilon) ball and has phase 1/2, contradicting the radius-1 circle constraint. Translation gives continuity everywhere. The Example interface is unchanged.
